one_liner: Track meal blocks/FLEX/dining dollars at 10 schools, scan receipts on-device, and get a Monte Carlo verdict on whether you'll run out before the semester ends.
problem: Dining apps show a balance but never whether it is enough; a $4k CMU plan is two currencies with different rules, so students either ration or hand $300 back in December.
target_user: College students on institutional meal plans (CMU, Pitt, Penn State, Temple, Penn, Drexel, Duquesne, Villanova, Lehigh, Rutgers).
core_loop: Pick school/plan (catalog from official pages with break calendars) -> log purchase by form, receipt photo (Tesseract + tender-line parser) or pasted Grubhub email -> localStorage or Supabase row -> per-bucket verdict, 2,000-run Monte Carlo band, today's meal-period plan, spend-by-place insights, plan advisor.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Sample-data generator (?demo) for judges; plan catalog hand-transcribed; Claude vision path present but switched off (DEFAULT_PROXY empty); CMU live hours from ScottyLabs API, other schools fixed lists; block values 'learned' only from receipts you feed it.
demo_risks: Low: static site works offline. Tesseract (~10 MB) loads from CDN on first scan and misreads crumpled receipts (results flagged 'check this'); Supabase sign-in and ScottyLabs API need network.
ui_experience: Four-tab dashboard (Home/Log/Eat/Plans) with school-colored badges, light/dark tokens, Chart.js actual/projected/ideal lines with shaded forecast band, guided 7-step tour, share-card canvas, phone bottom nav, installable PWA. Clean and readable; standard dashboard aesthetics.
physical_or_sensory: none (phone camera receipt scan is the only physical touch)
integrity_flags: 8 commits with real features (Phase 1 tracker, transaction log, 8 schools) timestamped 09:29-10:47 EDT Sept 19, before the 11:00 hacking start. Supabase publishable key committed (intended public). Claude/Anthropic receipt path exists as dead code despite No Wrapper framing.
ai_scaffolding_flags: .claude/launch.json only; DEVPOST.md polished. Docs far smaller than code (~6k lines JS).
novelty_notes: Budget-tracker category, but with several distinctive mechanisms: eating-days calendars from official academic calendars, a bucket model spanning ten schools' plan types, per-place block value learning, Monte Carlo resampling instead of a straight line, and zero-server OCR.
need_notes: Specific, relatable pain with concrete numbers ($4k/semester, $14.58/block) and anecdotal evidence; plan data sourced with URLs and verified dates.
wow_moment: Photograph a real thermal receipt on your phone and it logs '1 block + $2.75 FLEX' at the right cafe, then the home screen says 'FLEX: over 99% chance of running out, Nov 6-17'.
score_rationale: Common category with genuine twists (S1 5). Real student pain with data (S2 7). No Wrapper fit is solid (OCR + Monte Carlo, no LLM shipped) plus .Tech/DO (S3 6). Live, polished, tests, error states, offline (S4 13). Attractive but conventional dashboard, camera scan is the only tactile bit (S5 8). Wow is a mild 'neat'.
judge_summary: A very complete, live meal-plan tracker for ten schools with on-device receipt OCR and a Monte Carlo run-out forecast. Solid No Wrapper entry; not flashy. Note several feature commits landed ~90 minutes before the official start.

one_liner: Dry-run a draft loan agreement against what the bank can actually execute: Nemotron reads each clause, a deterministic capability-graph search returns PASS / MANUAL / FAIL with policy citations and a grounded redraft.
problem: Banks sign bespoke clauses (EUR 40M same-day, notice by 11:00, any office) that their cutoffs, funding windows and approvals cannot deliver, and only find out after signing.
target_user: Bank loan-operations / documentation analysts reviewing draft credit agreements before signature.
claimed_tracks: Beyond the Chatbot (NVIDIA Nemotron) - explicit 'What a chatbot can't do' section
core_loop: Drop/load the .md agreement packet -> parse + SHA-256 -> per clause POST /api/extract -> Nemotron JSON, Zod-validated with one retry, else labelled 'Cached' fixture -> evaluate.ts enumerates 32 routes x 14 comparators over capability graph v7/v8 -> finding cards with agreement vs policy passages -> Apply redraft and re-test, or switch bank state to v8; challenge mode grades raw-model answers against the engine.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Entire bank, agreement and capability graph are hand-written synthetic fixtures; only 4 of 32 clauses are checked; cached extractions recorded 2026-09-19 serve as fallback (labelled); reveal pacing is staged; reads only its own plain-text packet format (no PDF).
demo_risks: Low: NVIDIA free tier 429/503 degrades to labelled 'Cached' cards by design; Vercel-hosted; works with no key at all.
ui_experience: Single-screen React/Tailwind workbench: document pane with marked failing spans, four finding cards that reveal with path-search and typewriter animation, side-by-side agreement/bank quotes, redraft diff, Demo tools drawer with Nemotron call log, Export record. Professional and dense; text-heavy finance UI.
integrity_flags: README states first commit 13:33 EDT after start and discloses Codex + Claude use; commit log confirms. Seven AI-agent handoff docs in docs/. Devpost market figures self-flagged as unverified. No secrets.
ai_scaffolding_flags: docs/handoff-02..07 are explicit agent handoff briefs (timeboxes, 'top model for the API contract'); ~800 doc lines vs ~11k code lines, so code dominates.
novelty_notes: Loan operational-feasibility checking is a niche B2B problem most judges will not have seen; the LLM-extracts-but-never-decides architecture with a versioned capability graph and route search is a real mechanism, not a wrapper.
need_notes: Specific and credible (JPMorgan job title for the role, Citi $894M manual-error precedent), but evidence is author-asserted; solo hacker, no user quotes.
wow_moment: Open the FAIL card, press 'Apply and re-test' and the redrafted clause (every value copied from bank policy) flips to PASS; then switch the bank's approval register to v8 and the same clause moves FAIL -> MANUAL because Treasury renewed an authority.
score_rationale: Uncommon problem and a genuinely new mechanism (S1 8). Real, well-argued institutional pain but unverified figures (S2 7). Nails Beyond the Chatbot (clear role, challenge-mode eval, documented fallback) and stacks with Xtract/Compound (S3 8). Live, 224 tests, honest labelling, synthetic-only data (S4 13). Polished but dense text UI (S5 7). One clear 'huh' for finance judges.
judge_summary: Solo build that checks loan clauses against a synthetic bank's operating limits; Nemotron extracts, code decides, and a redraft re-tests to PASS live. Rigorous and honest, more impressive to a finance judge than a crowd.

one_liner: Two Python scripts that send basketball video clips to a Nemotron Nano 12B VL NIM and print JSON play-by-play.
problem: Not stated; implied: automatically log plays (shot/pass/rebound, player, outcome) from basketball footage.
target_user: Not stated; implied coaches or sports analysts.
core_loop: analyze-YT.py: yt-dlp download -> ffmpeg 20s/480p clips -> base64 video_url to NIM chat completion -> parse JSON array of plays -> plays.json. analyze-mp4.py: one clip straight to the NIM.
mocked_or_hardcoded: No outputs, results, UI or eval committed; assumes a Brev instance running the VL NIM; prompt-only structure with regex JSON salvage.
demo_risks: High: requires a GPU NIM endpoint and yt-dlp/ffmpeg; nothing to show but terminal JSON.
integrity_flags: Two commits: empty init at 10:52 and one 'Upload Project Files' at 04:19 Sept 20. No secrets. No README content, team, or track.
novelty_notes: Video-to-structured-events is a common VLM demo; basketball play logging is a mild angle but unexplored here.
need_notes: No user, problem, or evidence articulated.
wow_moment: None visible; at best a JSON list of plays printed from a clip.
score_rationale: Plausible idea with no articulation (S1 4, S2 3). Nemotron is used but its role, evidence and eval are absent (S3 2). Skeleton scripts only, unverifiable (S4 3). No UI (S5 0).
judge_summary: Two scripts that ask a Nemotron vision NIM to list basketball plays from a clip. No README, UI, results or evidence; effectively a starting point.

one_liner: A 3D traffic-redesign game on real OSM data of the Pitt campus: place crosswalks, bike lanes and road diets under a budget, run paired Monte Carlo (or SUMO) trials, and get a Gemini debrief spoken by ElevenLabs.
problem: Intersection safety vs throughput vs cost tradeoffs at Forbes/Bigelow, Fifth/Bigelow and Forbes/Bouquet are invisible to citizens and students; the game makes them tangible.
target_user: Students/citizens playing with campus intersections; loosely planners.
stack: Gemini 2.5 Flash with structured output + number verification
core_loop: Full-screen Three.js campus -> drag an upgrade onto a blue footprint (budget enforced) -> Run: local Monte Carlo surrogate in a web worker (or POST /api/simulation -> SUMO with matched seeds if DATABASE_URL + SUMO installed) -> before/after risk, delay, throughput, access, score -> Gemini debrief/coaching text -> optional spoken reply; game mode adds weather, closures, potholes, budgets; collision + fire replay, day/night, street-level walkthrough.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Default engine is 'local-network-surrogate-v1', explicitly uncalibrated (not SUMO, not crash prediction); traffic animation is illustrative; costs are planning allowances; SUMO study needs Postgres + SUMO and 'may take a few minutes'; Gemini falls back to canned text; voice answers are templates; no crash data reaches the frontend.
demo_risks: Moderate: heavy 3D scene on a laptop; SUMO/Tiger path unlikely to run on stage; Gemini quota; mic permission for voice. Core game works offline with the surrogate.
ui_experience: Rich: OSM-extruded campus (Cathedral of Learning, Towers), instanced facades, moving cars/bikes/PRT buses with brake lights, animated pedestrians who react to crashes, signal countdowns, weather particles and storm lighting, day/night clock, collision-and-fire replay with smoke, drag-and-drop tools with red/blue silhouettes, orbit/pan/street WASD navigation, walkthrough tutorial, Cantarell typography, dock panels. Judges can drag, run, and walk the street.
integrity_flags: Root README's 'Monte Carlo SUMO simulations' oversells the default surrogate (the frontend README is scrupulously honest). Only 20 commits with very large drops ('Final frontend'); data/sources docs for Argoverse/DENSO datasets that are never downloaded pad the scope. No secrets committed.
ai_scaffolding_flags: frontend/AGENTS.md working agreement; UX_AUDIT.md ends 'Final test results are recorded in the task completion message'; voice/ and gemini/ are self-contained agent-style modules with own venvs/tests. Docs are large but code (~2.7k dense JS lines, ~3k+ Python) is larger.
novelty_notes: SimCity-style intersection redesign on real Pittsburgh geometry with paired Monte Carlo and an optional true SUMO backend is uncommon at a hackathon; the honest data-provenance stance is unusual too.
need_notes: Pedestrian safety in Oakland is a real local issue and the data pipeline cites WPRDC/PennDOT/OSM, but the target user (player vs planner) is fuzzy and no user evidence is given.
wow_moment: Drag a raised crosswalk onto Forbes/Bigelow in a 3D Pitt campus, hit Run, watch cars queue and pedestrians cross, trigger a collision-and-fire replay, then hear the spoken debrief.
score_rationale: Fresh mechanism on real map data (S1 8). Real civic problem, fuzzy user (S2 6). Gemini and ElevenLabs are genuinely used with grounding checks, Tiger Data only in the optional path; voice is an add-on not voice-first (S3 6). Frontend loop works end to end with tests; SUMO/DB path optional and unproven on stage (S4 11). Visually striking, interactive 3D (S5 13).
judge_summary: A 3D SimCity-style sandbox of the Pitt campus where you buy crosswalks and bike lanes, run simulations, and watch traffic, weather and crashes play out, with Gemini text and ElevenLabs voice. Big, beautiful, and honest about its uncalibrated model.

one_liner: Scrapes Greenhouse/Lever job boards for six companies, computes 30-day hiring velocity, and has Nemotron write an 'analyst read' for investors while applicants rank the roles against a pasted resume.
problem: Job postings are a public signal of where a company is spending next; nobody turns them into a hiring-velocity read.
target_user: Investors/analysts (hiring signals) and job applicants (open roles ranked to a resume).
core_loop: ./gradlew ingest -> Greenhouse/Lever JSON -> Labeler (seniority/function/geo) -> SQLite first_seen/last_seen -> CompanyStats (last 30d vs prior 30d) + Detector rules -> InsightGeneratorService (Nemotron, cached by stats hash, deterministic fallback) -> InsightApiServer :8080 -> React #/investor cards and #/applicant list with in-browser term-overlap resume ranking.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Six hardcoded company boards; frontend shows labelled SAMPLE DATA (Cursor, Perplexity...) when backend is down; fallback 'Computed' reads without a key; resume match is naive keyword overlap; output.txt is a test model reply.
demo_risks: Moderate: needs JDK + Node, live scrape (~25 s), NVIDIA Ultra 550B reasoning calls (slow, truncation issues noted), two servers.
ui_experience: Three-page React UI with a cream applicant side and dark investor side, Manrope/DM Mono, cards with mix bars, trend badges and Computed/Nemotron labels. Neat but basic; no charts beyond bars.
integrity_flags: Compiled app/bin/*.class and output.txt committed; .idea/.vscode junk; polished README contrasts with chaotic commit history ('PLEASE', 'adding spooky stuff', 'first claude changes'). Directory still named awesomefinder (pivot). No secrets.
ai_scaffolding_flags: None beyond README style and a 'first claude changes' commit.
novelty_notes: Job-posting alt-data is a known concept (Revelio/Thinknum) but rare at hackathons; the dual applicant/investor framing is the twist.
need_notes: Plausible for investors, generic for applicants; no evidence, quotes or validation.
wow_moment: Open the investor view and read Nemotron's take on why Stripe posted 18 roles this month; paste a resume and see roles re-rank. Mild.
score_rationale: Common category with a twist (S1 5). Generic need, no evidence (S2 4). Nemotron only writes prose summaries of computed stats; no eval or comparison, so partial Beyond-the-Chatbot fit (S3 3). Pipeline coded end to end with fallbacks and unit tests but unverified live (S4 8). Basic web UI (S5 5).
judge_summary: A Java scraper plus React site that turns six companies' job boards into hiring-velocity stats and a Nemotron-written analyst blurb. Works in principle, honest about fallbacks, but little to see or touch.

one_liner: Your phone is the paddle: IMU swings drive a 120 Hz authoritative pickleball sim rendered first-person on a laptop, with Nemotron classifying shots and refereeing rallies against the rulebook, plus recorded referee voice.
problem: Play pickleball (and learn its rules) anywhere with just a phone and a laptop; no court, net or partner needed.
target_user: Casual players and gamers; dorm-room two-player LAN matches.
claimed_tracks: Beyond the Chatbot (explicit: 'Nemotron does real work here, not chatbot work')
core_loop: Phone DeviceMotion -> swing state machine/DTW -> ws 'swing' -> server physics at 120 Hz (hit window, bounces, NVZ, scoring) -> 60 Hz state broadcast -> laptop Three.js first-person court + bounce/racket audio; rally end -> rally envelope -> spawned python bridge -> Nemotron referee -> schema/score validation -> HUD ruling, evidence panel, referee mp3 clip; each swing -> classifier -> HUD shot/zone/confidence.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Live Nemotron gated by NEMOTRON_LIVE=1; otherwise heuristic classifier and state-machine referee labelled 'provisional/offline'. Eval results are OFFLINE only: state machine 50/50 on its own synthetic fixtures (0 human-reviewed), heuristic 43/50 on synthetic swings; rules.json 'reviewed_by' empty and the adapter refuses unreviewed config; serve-motion legality assumed; praise clips reserved.
demo_risks: High setup: mkcert CA trust on iPhone, same non-isolated Wi-Fi, iOS motion permission, MediaPipe CDN, python subprocess per call with 2.5 s timeouts, NVIDIA API. DEMO_SCRIPT lists keyboard/hotspot fallbacks.
ui_experience: Dark first-person 3D court with scoreboard HUD, serve dots, court minimap of tracked body position, phase indicator, referee evidence panel citing rules, shot analytics strip, background music, bounce and racket sounds, recorded referee voice ('fault red', 'out'). Physical swing input and camera tracking.
integrity_flags: Commits start 13:27 Sept 19; no secrets. Honest evidence labelling is a plus. ~1,700 lines of agent handoff/design docs (HANDOFF.md 'the previous agent already built', ARM_MOTION_HANDOFF, implementation-handoff, REVIEW_NOTES 'non-authoritative AI pre-review') against ~6k lines of code.
ai_scaffolding_flags: Multiple explicit AI-agent handoff documents and an AI pre-review; docs about 28% of code volume, not larger.
novelty_notes: Phone-as-motion-controller sports is a known genre, but an LLM referee that cites the 2026 USA Pickleball rulebook from an authoritative event log, plus IMU shot classification with a documented drop/dink confusion, is a distinct twist.
need_notes: Fun/fitness framing with no user evidence; the need is largely invented, though the rules-learning angle is plausible.
wow_moment: Swing your phone, the ball launches across a 3D court on the big screen with a thwack, the bot returns it, and a referee voice calls 'Fault, Red' while the evidence panel shows the bounce sequence and rule.
score_rationale: Known genre with an LLM-referee twist (S1 6). Invented need (S2 3). Nemotron roles are clear and an eval harness with documented failure exists, but live results were never run (S3 6). Game loop, multiplayer and physics tests work; live model path uncertain (S4 10). Physical, audible, 3D, judges can swing (S5 12). One strong wow.
judge_summary: Swing your phone and a 3D pickleball flies on the laptop, with a voice referee and Nemotron shot calls. Fun to try if the HTTPS/Wi-Fi setup survives the stage; the AI evaluation is honest but entirely offline.

one_liner: An ambient meeting teammate: listens via ElevenLabs Scribe, mints sticky-note cards for ideas with Nemotron, researches open questions with Claude sub-agents, and speaks up through a harness that only lets it talk when asked or when a finding lands.
problem: Working meetings lose ideas and threads, and nobody looks things up in the moment ('has anyone built this before?').
target_user: Small teams in brainstorming/working sessions (hackathon teams, product groups).
stack: Claude Agent SDK (front desk + WebSearch researchers)
ElevenLabs Scribe v2 realtime STT + streamed TTS
core_loop: Mic -> Scribe v2 -> append-only transcript.md -> Nemotron classifier every 2-5 s (new subject, addressed, questions, salience) -> placeholder card + signal; Nemotron notes agent rewrites notes.md every 20 s -> front desk (Claude Agent SDK) wakes with tools recall/investigate/say/note/working -> sub-agents web-search and write an HTML card page -> harness checks reason (asked/finding), budget, floor -> ElevenLabs TTS -> board over WebSocket.
mocked_or_hardcoded: fixtures/demo.txt scripted meeting replay and /inject text path for testing; browser STT fallback with nothing spoken when ElevenLabs key absent; research pinned to haiku/low effort; nothing else mocked.
demo_risks: High dependency: three external services (NIM had 55/208 calls needing retry in the eval run; ElevenLabs realtime; Claude Agent SDK needs the claude CLI logged in and 3-8 s tool loops), a noisy room, mic permission and echo. Text-injection fallback exists.
ui_experience: Paper-theme board: pastel square sticky notes with ruled lines that grow as people talk, a stop-motion sheep flock start screen, Board/Notes/Transcript views, thinking-level switch, investigations rail with timers, and a bottom strip of woke/said/hearing events with a highlighted spoken line. Distinctive, calm, and legible; judges can talk to it.
physical_or_sensory: audio (live voice in and spoken replies)
integrity_flags: First commit (23:51 Sept 19) ports 3,867 lines from a prior 'Heard! kitchen build' (STT/TTS, WebSocket hub, config, NIM client, board mic/audio helpers), i.e. roughly 40% of the Python is pre-existing; README discloses Claude Code authorship and commits carry Co-Authored-By. No secrets.
ai_scaffolding_flags: No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; docs/NEMOTRON.md is an eval write-up. Docs smaller than code (~5.4k lines).
novelty_notes: AI meeting notetakers are crowded (Otter, Granola), but an agent that mints cards live, dispatches research mid-meeting and interjects under a plain-code harness with 'fails toward silence' rules is a distinctive twist.
need_notes: Relatable, generic pain; no user evidence beyond the scripted demo, though the 'done before, 9+ times' finding is a compelling illustration.
wow_moment: Say 'Heard, has anyone built this before?' and a few seconds later a card reads 'DONE BEFORE, 9+ times' while the board speaks 'nine Devpost projects do this, plus Be My Eyes...' with a linked research page.
score_rationale: Crowded category, real twist (S1 6). Plausible but generic need (S2 5). Nails Beyond the Chatbot (clear split, six-config benchmark with latencies and documented failures) and is voice-first with ElevenLabs both ways (S3 8). Working loop with tests and eval, but three fragile services and ~40% ported code, no live URL (S4 11). Attractive, live, audible (S5 10).
judge_summary: A sticky-note board that listens to the meeting, files ideas as cards, researches them in the background and talks back when asked. Charming and well-evaluated on the Nemotron side; fragile on stage and partly built from a pre-hackathon base.

problem: Understanding a stock's valuation, growth and sentiment at a glance without reading filings.
claimed_tracks: Beyond the Chatbot implied ('the track's Nemotron-on-NVIDIA story' in .env.example; original README: 'built on NVIDIA's Nemotron')
core_loop: Ticker search -> /api/analysis (Yahoo quoteSummary) -> metric cards, price chart, rec trend, news -> /api/analysis/sentiment: SEC brief + insider Form 4 + headlines -> Nemotron JSON (zod, one repair retry, quota backoff, 6 h cache) -> AI outlook card; /api/compare/verdict picks A vs B; /api/industry screens; /api/chat streams.
mocked_or_hardcoded: No mocks; depends entirely on live Yahoo (unofficial) and EDGAR; hasLlmKey guards only; v0.app placeholder assets in public/; comments cite a PLAN doc not in the repo.
demo_risks: Moderate-high: unofficial Yahoo API breakage/rate limits, NVIDIA free-tier request limits (retries added), Ultra 550B reasoning latency (maxDuration 300 s), no live URL committed.
ui_experience: Polished generic shadcn dashboard: hero search, module cards, market movers, metric lists, recharts price history, recommendation trend, compare grid with verdict, industry tabs, chat box. Attractive SaaS look, dark mode; nothing interactive beyond search/tabs.
integrity_flags: README and LICENSE deleted in the 'potential frontend added' commit; no README at HEAD. Layout declares generator 'v0.app' and routes log '[v0]' - UI scaffold generated by v0 with placeholder images. Commits start 11:44 after start. No secrets.
ai_scaffolding_flags: v0-generated starter; 'Exclude codebase survey from the repo' commit; PLAN section references. No CLAUDE.md.
novelty_notes: LLM stock-analysis dashboards are seen many times; SEC XBRL + Form 4 grounding and the 'prefer SEC over market estimates' rule is a modest twist.
need_notes: Generic retail-investor need; no evidence or user.
wow_moment: Nemotron's verdict cites a 10-K revenue figure and flags insider open-market sells on the compare page. Mild.
score_rationale: Well-worn category with a grounding twist (S1 3). Generic need (S2 3). Nemotron does structured, grounded analysis but also a chat box, and there is no eval or comparison (S3 4). Fairly complete multi-page app with real data paths, caching and retries, but no README, tests or live link (S4 10). Polished template dashboard (S5 7).
judge_summary: A clean v0-scaffolded stock dashboard where Nemotron writes SEC-grounded verdicts and comparisons. Competent and complete-ish, but a familiar idea with nothing to touch and no README.

one_liner: Receive and reply to Gmail over a Meshtastic LoRa mesh with no cellular or Wi-Fi at the far end, using a custom compressed 200-byte packet codec and an off-grid inbox UI.
problem: Email is unreachable without internet; LoRa mesh radios can carry tiny packets for miles if mail is shrunk and chunked.
target_user: People off-grid or in outages (hikers, disaster responders, rural users) who still need email.
stack: zlib raw deflate with shared dictionary
stdlib HTTP server + plain HTML/JS inbox (older Streamlit UI)
LilyGO T-Beam S3 LoRa nodes on stock firmware
core_loop: MessagePing polls Gmail history -> MessageTransform -> MeshCodec.to_packets strips quotes/URLs, deflates with DICT, chunks to <=200 B with id/part/total header -> MeshSend paced on the radio's real TX queue -> LoRa private channel -> end node -> station.py reassembles, requests missing parts, decodes -> endpoint/server.py JSON API -> web inbox; replies/compose travel back as OUTBOUND packets and MessageReply sends via Gmail.
mocked_or_hardcoded: MockRadio loopback via a spool folder and a 'demo' transport with sample mail; README status admits the gateway loop joining Gmail to the radio and the phone app are 'not built yet' (MyApplication/ holds only .idea); range untested (nodes side by side); Windows Bluetooth hangs.
demo_risks: Moderate: needs two T-Beams with antennas on the right region/channel, USB ports, Gmail OAuth on the gateway, ~2 s airtime per packet; loopback/demo modes as fallback.
ui_experience: Dark glassy Mesh Mail inbox (plain HTML/JS): live-connection pill, transport selector listing real COM ports, threads, compose/reply, real packet-progress bar. Basic but tidy. The radios themselves are the visual.
integrity_flags: projectContext.txt calls it a firmware fork; README correctly says stock firmware. Commit names 'Betterified the entire codebase', 'The 20 minute prooompt', two 'Revert to state at...' commits suggest LLM rewrites and rollbacks. Secrets (channel.url, secrets.json, tokens) correctly gitignored. Commits start 11:29 after start.
ai_scaffolding_flags: projectContext.txt is a prompt-context file; commit messages reference prompting. Docs are small relative to ~2.8k lines of code.
novelty_notes: Email over LoRa mesh is uncommon at hackathons and needs real engineering (dictionary compression, chunk/reassembly, retransmit requests, airtime pacing) with physical radios.
need_notes: Off-grid comms is a real need (disasters, backcountry), though email specifically is slightly contrived; no evidence or users given.
wow_moment: Send yourself an email, watch the gateway laptop chunk it into ~70 bytes, and seconds later it appears in an inbox on an air-gapped laptop wired only to a blinking LoRa radio, then reply back through the mesh.
score_rationale: Uncommon problem with a real mechanism (S1 8). Real but under-evidenced need (S2 5). Strong No Wrapper fit: no LLM, explainably hard, physical demo (S3 7). Codec, radio send, reassembly and reply exist and reportedly ran on hardware, but the README admits gaps and the phone app is absent (S4 9). Physical radios plus a modest web inbox (S5 9).
judge_summary: Email squeezed into 200-byte LoRa packets and read on an internet-less laptop through two Meshtastic radios, with replies going back. Genuinely hard, physical, no LLM; rough edges and no phone app yet.
